title: Parental Mutual Support During Cancer (ElternMUT): Development and Evaluation of a Psycho-Oncological Group Intervention for Parents with Cancer
summary:
This study develops and evaluates a psycho-oncological group intervention to support parents with cancer who have minor children. The primary aim of the study is to examine whether this group intervention is feasible and is accepted by participants and perceived as helpful.
Participants will attend three group sessions addressing topics such as coping with distress, age-appropriate communication with children, recognizing and addressing different needs, and typical reactions of children. Questionnaires will be completed before and after participation in order to assess changes.
conditions: Psycho-oncological burden in the family context: parents with cancer who have minor children

interventions.name: Single-arm, prospective, monocentric, uncontrolled psycho-oncological group intervention consisting of three sessions of 120 minutes each, conducted at approximately biweekly intervals, preceded by an initial consultation. Each group will include approximately 8 participants, with a maximum of 12. T

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Fluency in the German language 
•	Ability to participate in the three group sessions (held biweekly) 
•	Written informed consent following prior information 

Inclusion criteria for the affected parent:
o	Cancer patient with any type of cancer 
o	< 6 months since initial diagnosis 
o	Has minor children 

Inclusion criteria for the healthy parent:
o	Partner of a cancer patient
Exclusion criteria:
•	Severe psychiatric disorders and suicidality 
•	Severe cognitive impairment
